nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: N/A
nodes.eventDescription: The likelihood of anyone surviving the spaceship's destruction is low but not zero: Zephyrus had self-propelled emergency escape pods and shuttles distributed throughout the ship for evacuation. Someone could have reached them just in time. But what exactly could destroy Zephyrus, our most advanced and well-protected spaceship? Could the Behemoth be next? Learning more about what happened might increase the chances of survival for this ship and its crew. For that, the flight recorder and the bridge voice recorder must be retrieved.

actions.description: Harsh conditions jam the long-distance signals. To pick up the emergency signal from the escape pods, a more powerful transmitter is required.
actions.resultDescription: The transmitter has picked up several signals, all heavily distorted. For now, it is unclear whether any of them belong to an escape pod, but Mnemosyne will work on finding out.

actions.description: Mnemosyne can analyze all the recorded data of the Zephyrus's destruction and predict the probable crash sites of its debris, including the pieces where the orange box (flight recorder) should be contained.
actions.resultDescription: Mnemosyne is about to determine a possible crash site area of the mothership's fragment containing the Orange box. The fragment is still in orbit and has yet to pass through the lower atmosphere, shattering in the process and thus complicating the precise prediction of the orange box's final location.

nodes.title: The Moment After the End

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.spawnConditions: On an island with additional escape pod model.
nodes.eventIntro: An escape pod must be somewhere on this island, as this is where its distress signal is coming from.
nodes.eventDescription: Blood, claw marks, shredded EVAs, guts, torn limbs, and more blood greet your scouts inside the escape pod. Something has gotten to the space refugees before you.

actions.description: Arm the scouts and send them to search the island for survivors (or their bodies).
actions.resultDescription:
Despite the lack of progress in locating people from Zephyrus, the scouts have had significant success in finding the predators, possibly responsible for attacking the escape pod. All they had to do was stay on the island long enough to become bait for the hungry beasts.
 The ambush left two of the party severely wounded, but the team managed to fight off and retreat to the extraction point, leaving the island without discovering the fate of the survivors.

actions.description: Investigate the scene to gather clues, recreate the events, and learn more about the fate of the survivors.
actions.resultDescription: The escape pod's log accounts for six passengers, one of them is a child. The shredded EVAs and most of the blood belong to two adults, which leaves four people missing. But where would they go?   That's when the scouts notice another clue. Each escape pod, specifically designed for Keeling in mind, is equipped with a lifeboat in case the landing happens to be 'watering.' And such a lifeboat is currently missing from the escape pod's inventory.

nodes.location: On an island with additional escape pod model.
nodes.title: The Moment After the End

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: According to Mnemosyne's predictions, the section of the mothership containing the orange box should have landed on this island.
nodes.eventDescription:
The scouts follow the column of smoke that echoes the trajectory of the fallen fragment. The closer they get, the more destruction they see. The blast from the impact has melted stone and banished the living elements from the location. Not a blade of grass has remained. Just pockmarks from stone-turned-shrapnel everywhere, leaving long-standing scars.
 And then, a crater. A large, smoldering chunk of twisted metal lies inside. The dispatched scouts approach a burial ground of their mothership, watching it somberly — another reminder of what they have lost.

actions.description: Six hours of painstaking and careful "surgery" are required to extract the orange box without any risk of damaging it.
actions.resultDescription: Slowly and carefully, like handling a bomb that is one wrong move away from exploding, the team peels off layer after layer of metal, exposing a mess of fried spaceship's innards. They manage to extract many components and useful implements, but not the one you hoped to find.  The orange box is not here, and it never has been. A different fragment must have carried it down here. Mnemosyne will have to do the math all over again, update her calculations, and give you a new (and this time correct and final) location of the orange box.

actions.description: We have no time to waste on the surgical dissection. We need the orange box, and we need it ASAP.
actions.resultDescription:
Tuuli, Chief Engineer, does her best to calculate the amount of explosive materials as well as their placement to keep the further destruction of Zephyrus's wreck under control. Despite her best efforts, all the fine elements of the spaceship that could have survived the fall are now beyond salvation.
      Luckily, the orange box isn't there. It never has been. A different fragment must have carried it down. Mnemosyne will have to do the math all over again, update her calculations, and give you a new (and this time correct and final) location of the orange box.

nodes.title: The Moment After the End

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: Repelled by the overwhelming numbers of local predators, the scouts failed to discover the fate of the survivors. It is the time to learn from our mistakes and attempt again.
nodes.eventDescription: The island is swarming with dangerous predators. And somewhere, surrounded by violent beasts, a group of survivors might still be alive. Or so many of your crew want to believe.

actions.description: The drones should not attract the unwanted attention of local predators and will therefore traverse the island more efficiently.
actions.resultDescription:
As expected, the drones are of no interest to the carnivores and pass through the island without a hitch. But after hours of circling around, they find no evidence of any human being present in this place.

Eventually, passing by the escape pod one more time, one of the operators notices that a lifeboat is missing. And since animals don't usually sail on boats, it can mean only one thing...

actions.description: Protected by force shields, an armed group can easily dispatch the hunting packs of predators and provide the necessary aid to survivors if any are found.
actions.resultDescription: The scouts move swiftly through the island, unhindered. Claws and fangs fail to pierce the force fields encompassing the bodies of the scouts, while the bullets find no such problem with the animal hides.  But all that bloodshed leads to nothing. Your scouts find no survivors on the island, nor their remains.  But when they pass by the escape pod one more time, they realize that it does not have the emergency lifeboat. And since animals don't usually sail on boats, it can mean only one thing...

nodes.title: The Moment After the End

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: The lifeboat is feverishly tossed around by the legion of turbulent waves.
nodes.eventDescription: Your scouts reach the lifeboat and meet the survivors. But it is not the reunion they have been hoping for.  People on the lifeboat look horrible. Their eyes bulge in pain, rimmed by blood. Crimson tears run down and spread, like Martian deltas, on their puffed, inflamed faces.

actions.description: Bring the survivors to the ship and provide them with all the necessary medical help.
actions.resultDescription:
The scouts return with the blood-crying survivors, and the fight for their lives begins.

Based on the preliminary examination, the virus appears to be a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It is much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More work needs to be done to better understand its properties, learn how it ended up on Keeling, and find a way to treat it.

actions.description: Keep the survivors on the lifeboat and examine the virus there, thus avoiding any unnecessary risks for the crew on the Behemoth.
actions.resultDescription: R&D scientists and doctors give instructions to the scouts. They examine the survivors, collect the samples for R&D analysis, and do what they can to help. In the end, nothing works, and the scouts give the final gift to the tormented people — painkillers.  Having taken all the necessary precautions, the scouts then deliver the samples to the R&D lab for further research.  The virus appears to be a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It is much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More research is needed to better understand its properties and how it ended up on Keeling.

nodes.title: The Moment After the End

nodes.name: The Moment After the End
nodes.eventIntro: The lifeboat is tossed around by the legion of turbulent waves. Radio silence greets your ship.
nodes.eventDescription:
Bodies of the survivors, who are survivors no more, cover the floor of the lifeboat's only cabin. Their eyes bulge in pain, rimmed by a dried moat of blood. Crimson tears have run down and spread, like Martian deltas, on their puffed, still inflamed faces. These people have fled from horrible death in space and on the island, only to succumb to a no less cruel disease.  Among those corpses also lies the frail body of a child.

It is not Liora.

actions.description: Send scouts to take the samples for the R&D lab.
actions.resultDescription: Having taken all the necessary precautions, the scouts extract the samples and deliver them to the R&D lab for further research. Mars Abbadie, the Head of R&D, contacts you later with preliminary results. The virus is a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It is much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More research is needed to better understand its properties and how it ended up on Keeling.

actions.description: The examination must be conducted remotely using drones.
actions.resultDescription: Transmitted results indicate that the virus responsible for the death of survivors is a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It appears to be much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative. More research is needed to better understand its properties and how it ended up on Keeling.

nodes.eventIntro: Another mangled piece of Zephyrus has found its way down into the waters of Keeling.
nodes.eventDescription: The fallen fragment of Zephyrus is the epicenter of mass destruction, surrounded by a field of dead, boiled fish bobbing on the disturbed water.  For now, it stays on the surface, but eventually its weight will drive it down to the bottom, making the retrieval of the orange box much more complicated.

actions.description: The extraction team requests a Tricoder. It is a highly versatile scanning device that can detect, analyze, and predict a wide array of information. It should be indispensable for navigating a compromised structure.
The team has to manage without a tricorder.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: So, captain… What should we do next?
nodes.eventDescription: At least that explains the time loop. But we need to choose a course of action to break it, preferably with Zephyrus still in one piece.

actions.description: There are other Primordial structures on Keeling. To understand their technology, we must first study it.
actions.resultDescription: We spotted several structures that can be identified as potentially built by the Primordials. They are all in close proximity and potentially reachable by our means of transportation.

actions.description: First, we must find out who destroyed Zephyrus and why.
actions.resultDescription: We have detected several large fragments of Zephyrus nearby. Maybe we could retrieve the Orange box or, at least, examine the debris to learn what type of damage the ship suffered.

actions.description: As we previously found out, the attack could be preceded by sabotage.
actions.resultDescription: We have detected several large fragments of Zephyrus nearby. Maybe we could examine them to learn more about what caused such gruesome damage.

nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: Approaching the Primordial structure.
nodes.eventDescription: The complex is built on the floating island. We detect an unknown type of EM-field surrounding the structures.

actions.description: Ask for volunteers. Give them the best protection gear we can provide. We have no time to waste.
actions.resultDescription: Scouts managed to stay there only briefly before their protection began to fail.  They managed to escape, taking with them several slabs of an Eldritium, a rare metal. It probably was mined or refined there. Unfortunately, they also carried radiation sickness.

actions.description: This looks dangerous. We should investigate before putting our scouts at risk.
actions.resultDescription: We still don’t exactly understand what this field is or what its purpose is. But now we know the possible hazards and how to avoid them.

actions.description: Using the gathered information, we can providereliable protection for our scouts.
actions.resultDescription: The scouts still have precious little time to explore the complex. Presumably, it was a refinery for Eldritium, with a significant supply of the material still there. Scouts couldn’t take all, but gathered data about the industrial capacities of the Primordials.

nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: Approaching the Primordial structure.
nodes.eventDescription: This looks more like a spacecraft than a marine building. Or even a space station. Crash-landed in these shallows.

actions.description: Despite the sorry state of the structure, we might recover artifacts
actions.resultDescription: Turns out, this was a space station, orbiting the Keeling some centuries, if not millennia ago. Most of the tech here is beyond our understanding, and the in a sorry state because of its age and conditions, but despite that, the scouts retrieved several artifacts. This may be the first step to a real breakthrough.

actions.description: The structure doesn’t look stable. We’ll be putting our crew at risk, sending them without any prior exploration.
actions.resultDescription: Surprisingly, the structure still holds. Now we can clearly tell it was a large orbital station, which, for some reason, left the orbit and landed in the shallows of this archipelago. There is structural damage here and there, but mostly the station is intact. Whatever caused the station to fall didn’t destroy it. We can proceed with the scouting team.

actions.description: Now, when we are sure the place is safe, we can send our scouts.
actions.resultDescription: This was a space station, orbiting the Keeling some centuries, if not millennia ago. Most of the tech here is beyond our understanding, and the in a sorry state because of its age and conditions, but despite that, the scouts retrieved several artifacts. This may be the first step to a real breakthrough.

nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: Approaching the Primordial structure.
nodes.eventDescription: The structure is in very bad shape. Once levitating, it is now half-buried in the soil and heavily damaged.

actions.description: Scanners show no life or energy signatures. The place is dead. We can send the team in.
actions.resultDescription: The place was pillaged a long time ago. Everything was either looted, smashed, or turned to rust & dust. All we can extract from here is some basic materials.

actions.description: We need archeologists here, not looters. We must act carefully.
actions.resultDescription:
The place was pillaged a long time ago. However, the scientists manage to gather intel about the pillagers. This was a native Keeling civilization, primitive but resourceful, capable of recycling the tech, not only extracting precious metals and gems from it. It also seems that they didn’t quite finish their business here. There may be something of value still hidden there.
They went on, but to no avail. Yet just as the search began to look futile, archeologists found a hidden chamber with a strange device, possibly still functional.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: Zephyrus fragment spotted
nodes.eventDescription: This fragment has traces of an explosion. A careful study can unveil the details of the attack. However, the fragment is small and badly damaged. We aren’t likely to find any surviving data or gear here.

actions.description: Investigation may take precious time, but it’s the only way to find out how the ship was destroyed.
actions.resultDescription: The investigation showed that the explosion was outward, not inward. Which means that something exploded inside the ship. Whether as the result of sabotage or because of some alien technology, causing some internal devices to explode is yet unclear.

actions.description: Time is of the essence. A quick check will do. We know the weapon was of devastating power, so the knowledge won’t save us from it anyhow.
actions.resultDescription: No luck. The fragment is burned out to ash, leaving nothing of value. We managed to retrieve just a small quantity of rare metals.

actions.description: We can base the investigation on the Orange box data to add more pieces to this puzzle.
actions.resultDescription: The investigation showed that the explosion was outward, not inward. Which means that something exploded inside the ship. The Orange box data shows the critical malfunction in the battery block safety systems in this sector of the ship, seconds before the explosion. Further study is required to clarify the connection between these two occurrences.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: All the points of interest are checked. We can start the research.
nodes.eventDescription: Gathered artifacts and data can tell us more about the Primordials, their motives, and their current state.

actions.description: We only managed to scratch the surface here. More information will be needed to obtain a deeper understanding of the Primordials, but it’s a start.
actions.resultDescription: Despite the first meeting with the Prims, all the structures we’ve found were deserted many centuries ago. What was the creature the Captain spoke to? A ghost? Or maybe they moved on – deeper into the sea perhaps? However, we didn’t find anything that could help us with the riddle of the Prism. We must continue our search.

actions.description: We’ve gathered a lot of data. The Primordials are an advanced and mysterious species, but this research may become a first step in understanding their motives.
actions.resultDescription: We had a first contact, but what was the creature that contacted us? All the structures we explored, even those that were still functioning, were deserted ages ago! Yet, the artifacts we’ve found and the processed data show the possibility of the multidimensional technology being used by the Primordals. However, such tech might require huge amounts of energy. How the Prism is functioning without the potent energy source, and whether there is a limit to its uses, remains unknown.

actions.description: We managed to gather a massive amount of data to research. The main problem now is how to process it.
actions.resultDescription: The data shows that the first contact we had wasn’t a direct contact. At least not as direct as we thought it was. The Primodial wasn’t there in full, and we aren’t even sure that he could be present in a full material form. The one Voss talked to could be either an AI avatar, a transdimensional projection, or even an interactive semi-intelligent recording of the person long gone. The artifacts collected are mostly functional and can be studied to gain a better understanding of the prims’ technology, especially the Prism. What we know now is that the Prism is autonomous and powered by the source beyond our 4 dimensions. All attempts to mess with it will lead to the safety reboot, as well as any serious damage to the ship and crew. We can’t help but wonder: could Zephyrus survive the attack if the Prism were still aboard it?

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: Zephyrus fragment spotted
nodes.eventDescription: This fragment is badly damaged, but the damage itself is a bit strange. A closer look shows that the wreck was looted by someone.

actions.description: Have to be quicker next time. Let's retrieve what we can and move on.
actions.resultDescription: The looters were there, and now they are gone. They took almost everything of value. At least all that survived the crash.  All that is left for us is just the basic materials like metal and plastic.

actions.description: Secure the wreck in case the looters are still around and then extract the valuables.
actions.resultDescription:
Whoever did this has some industrial equipment. Not that advanced, but effective. We found some remnants of it: broken parts, exhausted batterys etc. The looters took all they could, even the metal plates that they managed to tear off. They had to have a large vessel to carry all that of the island. Also they picked up all the surviving electronics for some reason.
Were they just occasional marauders or intently covered the tracks of the attack?
One of them lost some kind of decoration, abadge or something. Maybe it will guide us to the marauders in the future.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: Zephyrus fragment spotted
nodes.eventDescription: This fragment had sunken by the time we arrived, but scanners detected a strange signal nearby.

actions.description: The waters are shallow here. Maybe we can use divers to reach the Fragment?
actions.resultDescription: No use. Our divers reached the fragment but barely had time to explore it. The local fauna is very aggressive there, so they had to withdraw soon. Still, they managed to recover a data cluster.

actions.description: It might be just our luck, but we should definitely check it.
actions.resultDescription: We found an alien device, damaged by the impact of the fragment’s fall. The device is not functioning, but the examination proves it was a powerful jamming device, perhaps one of those that interfered with the signal from Zephyrus. Hard to tell who built it: the tech is clearly alien and relatively complex.

nodes.name: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.title: Once More Into The Frey
nodes.eventIntro: The R&D formed a task force to study the Explosion
nodes.eventDescription: The data gathered from the damaged Zephyrus fragment could shed some light on the circumstances of the Zephyrus destruction

actions.shortDescription: Investigate the source of the explosion
actions.description: Action description...

lines.text: Captain, with all due respect, looking for survivors should be our highest priority. This is the only humane option we have.
Captain, we've located the lifeboat within comm link reach.
Finally... let me speak to them.
This is Elias Voss, captain of BCEV-07M. Can someone hear me?
Oh, thank goodness... We contracted something on that island. It hurts so much.
The lifepod's log states there was a child on board...
I wasn't the only parent back on Zephyrus. It means nothing.
Listen... is it true that there is a child with you?
Yes, I've got my daughter here.
That's the thing—it shouldn't have happened! The virus couldn't have bypassed their suits.
So we're not going to have our brains bleed out of our eyes. That's nice.
I believe it was a bioweapon.
Captain, we got the orange box! But... it doesn't have anything about the last ten minutes.
Inside job?
I can't see how an outside force could have paralyzed Zephyrus's entire nervous system.
Lifepods are supplied with everything their passengers might need for weeks. The orange box, however, could be hopelessly lost unless we act.
Captain, the transmitter has detected a signal awfully similar to the frequency our escape shuttles and pods use.
We must check it out then. Add its location to the navigation panel.
Right away!
And, Captain?
What?
I just wanted to say, you know, you shouldn't lose hope just yet.
Stop. That's enough.
Why? Zephyrus had enough pods for mass evacuation.
I'm afraid to get my hopes up...
...afraid to feel the heartbreak again...
...losing her again and again, each time I open the escape pod and she's not there...
It's easier to accept, just in case.
I must say I'm surprised by your decision. I thought you would make us overturn every slab of metal from Zephyrus, just to be sure.
And I am not the only one. Many are... disappointed.
And what about you? Disappointed, as well?
I... I understand your point of view. But are you yourself on board with what you are doing?
Mis right. We must know what happened to Zephyrus.
I can see there's something else you're not saying.
It's just...
I'm done lying to myself.
Liora couldn't have reached the emergency bay in time. Every upturned slab, every lifepod without her inside would...
...would kill me.
No point in chasing ghosts. No, I want to know what happened, and if there is someone — keyword, someone responsible for this.
I'd like to sweep the area. And, considering the violence those people met here, I believe it is only reasonable to request firearms.
The lifepod's log states there was a child on board...
I wasn't the only parent back on Zephyrus. It means nothing.
I see it in your eyes: it means a lot.

Yes. 

I'm terrified.
Captain, we've got an incoming transmission from the lifeboat.
Finally... let me speak to them. This is Elias Voss, the captain of BCEV-07M, speaking. Can someone hear me?
Is... is this real? Or am I... imagining this?
I reassure you, this is quite true. We've come to help you.
Oh, thank goodness.
Listen... is it true that then is a child with you?
Survivor (generic icon): Yes, I've got my daughter here.
Your daughter? I... I see.
Um, listen, you have doctors on the ship, right?
Is someone hurt?
We think we've... um, contracted something on that island. We're not feeling too well. Please, help us. It hurts so much.
Let's stay focused on the pod. The Reckon Craft cargo space is limited and we will need all the gear we can get.
Commander, the beacon frequency matches pre-collapse naval telemetry. Proceed with caution.
Contact with Zephyrus is lost, Captain. Visual analysis suggests it has been destroyed. Calculating potential casualties...
With all likelihood, there is little to no chance of survivors.
No...
No, it... it can't be...
Captain, per protocol, you are now in charge of the entire mission.
Captain?
Just...
Just give a moment...
Unfortunately, this is an emergency, and therefore, not an appropriate time for a ‘moment.’
Now, shall we review all the possible courses of action available?
I'm ready when you are.
Captain, I have completed my analysis and added the expected location of the flight recorder to the navigation panel.
Thank you, M.
I also wanted to discuss the recent decrease in crew morale. An unhappy crew leads to complications. Did you consider giving a motivational speech?
To give a good speech, one must believe in what gospels he's spewing. Me? I don't know that I do. Besides, I hate giving speeches. I'm the man of action, preferring the results to speak for myself.
No speech? Alright.
You must try to meet some of their needs then: to reinforce their sense of security.
I'll keep it in mind.
Captain, I've established the location of the bridge voice recorder. Adding it to your navigation panel!
Thanks, M.
Captain, with all due respect, but it is not too late to turn back and start looking for the survivors.
Believe me, I do not forget, not for a moment, about those people. But first, we must—
Why?! What does it change? Help me understand, ‘cause I can't see why we would choose an obituary over people's lives!

I'm doing it for the crew! Zephyrus traversed lightyears of void, passed asteroid fields, escaped black holes, all to be annihilated just outside this Primordial planet... If there's someone or something responsible for what happened... we must know.
What can just one ship do?
We'll find the way. End of the discussion.
Tuuli, tell me you can restore some of the data from the recorder.
Oh, I can... ...just not about the last hours of Zephyrus. That information is gone for good.
Was it our fault?
I can't tell. The casing was ruptured. The contents damaged. Could've happened at various points of its fall.
Is there anything... anything at all that we can learn?
Only that there was nothing abnormal in the ship's systems two days before. If it were a malfunction, it must've manifested itself today.
I see. M, I need you to start calculating the bridge voice recorder’s location. We need more information.
Right away, sir.
Abbadie, have you found anything yet?
Yes. I'm uploading everything to your database.
Give me a summary.
Seven minutes before the end: the communication network suffers a series of malfunctions, basically leaving the threat-detection system mute.
Five minutes before the end: several data concentrators stop routing their signals. Both external and internal monitoring devices are cut off.
And that's it. The ship's nervous system was basically disabled.
Sounds way too consistent for random malfunctions... an outside job?
It was done from inside.
But... who would sabotage their own ship?
I... I don't know. Maybe the bridge voice recorder can tell us more.
Right... M, I need the location of the other recorder.
Of course, sir.

Immediately after the drop, the cutscene with the destruction of Zepyrus triggers. The following dialogue describes the shock the team fell into, completely dazed by their sudden time loop. It takes effort to overcome the shock and start doing something.  As this was the first return, the dialogues must demonstrate the confusion and surprise
Key Event marker spawns on the island with the Primordial structure. Scouting the event triggers the cutscene in which Voss meets the Primordials. After the cutscene ends, the 0A Event triggers.
